evaluations.citation: ACI 301-20 §4 and ACI 305.1-14 §3.2–3.3 limit maximum concrete temperature to 95 °F (35 °C) at time of discharge; a higher temperature is permitted only with successful past field experience or preconstruction testing and prior approval of the architect/engineer. ACI 305R plastic-shrinkage guidance sets an evaporation-rate precaution threshold of 0.2 lb/ft²/hr (0.1 lb/ft²/hr for low-bleed mixes). constraints.label: ACI 305 evaporation rate ≤ 0.2 lb/ft²/hr
constraints.citation_fragment: Precautions against plastic shrinkage cracking are required when the calculated evaporation rate reaches 0.2 lb/ft²/hr (1.0 kg/m²/h) for conventional concrete, and 0.1 lb/ft²/hr (0.5 kg/m²/h) for low-bleed mixes such as Type 1L blended cements. FHWA states that at ≥ 1.0 kg/m²/h 'definite action to retard evaporation is necessary'. NJDOT MP 29-08 requires placement to be discontinued when the evaporation rate reaches or exceeds 0.15 lb/ft²/hr.

evaluations.citation: ACI 301-20 §4 and ACI 305.1-14 §3.2–3.3 limit maximum concrete temperature to 95 °F (35 °C) at time of discharge; a higher temperature is permitted only with successful past field experience or preconstruction testing and prior approval of the architect/engineer. ACI 305R plastic-shrinkage guidance sets an evaporation-rate precaution threshold of 0.2 lb/ft²/hr (0.1 lb/ft²/hr for low-bleed mixes). evaluations.verdict_summary: Concrete masonry — hot weather construction: 8.5 h bar at 10:12 clips the window 00:00–00:00 (72 h open). Binding constraint: Hot-weather procedures triggered above 37.8 °C (100 °F).
evaluations.citation: TMS 602 / ACI 530.1 hot weather construction requirements as summarised in Brick Industry Association Technical Note 1, Tables 2a/2b: preparation and construction procedures are triggered above 100 °F (37.8 °C) or above 90 °F (32.2 °C) with a wind speed greater than 8 mph — 'maintain sand piles in a damp, loose condition; maintain temperature of mortar and grout below 120 °F; use mortar within 2 hours of initial mixing'; protection requires 'fog spray all newly constructed masonry until damp, at least three times a day until the masonry is three days old'. A second tier applies above 115 °F (46.1 °C) or above 105 °F (40.6 °C) with wind greater than 8 mph.
evaluations.standard_ref: TMS 602 / ACI 530.1 / ASCE 6 Article 1.8 C — Hot Weather Construction (via BIA Technical Note 1)
evaluations.advisory_notice: Advisory and contractual. Does not replace the field measurement the referenced standard requires.

constraints.label: Hot-weather procedures triggered above 37.8 °C (100 °F)
constraints.citation_fragment: TMS 602 hot weather requirements are triggered 'above 100 °F (37.8 °C) or above 90 °F (32.2 °C) with a wind speed greater than 8 mph'.

constraints.label: Wind-modified hot-weather trigger (this is why wind matters, not just heat)
constraints.citation_fragment: Tier 1 — above 100 °F, or above 90 °F with wind > 8 mph: maintain sand piles damp and loose, keep mortar and grout below 120 °F, use mortar within 2 hours of initial mixing, fog spray newly constructed masonry until damp at least three times a day until the masonry is three days old. Tier 2 — above 115 °F, or above 105 °F with wind > 8 mph: additionally shade materials and mixing equipment from direct sunlight and use cool mixing water; ice is permitted provided it is melted when added.

constraints.label: Wind-modified hot-weather trigger (this is why wind matters, not just heat)
constraints.citation_fragment: Tier 1 — above 100 °F, or above 90 °F with wind > 8 mph: maintain sand piles damp and loose, keep mortar and grout below 120 °F, use mortar within 2 hours of initial mixing, fog spray newly constructed masonry until damp at least three times a day until the masonry is three days old. Tier 2 — above 115 °F, or above 105 °F with wind > 8 mph: additionally shade materials and mixing equipment from direct sunlight and use cool mixing water; ice is permitted provided it is melted when added.

evaluations.verdict_summary: Cast-in-place concrete — hot weather placement: 9.3 h bar at 12:00 clips the window 20:00–07:00 (11 h open). Binding constraint: Concrete temperature at discharge ≤ 35 °C (95 °F).
evaluations.citation: ACI 301-20 §4 and ACI 305.1-14 §3.2–3.3 limit maximum concrete temperature to 95 °F (35 °C) at time of discharge; a higher temperature is permitted only with successful past field experience or preconstruction testing and prior approval of the architect/engineer. ACI 305R plastic-shrinkage guidance sets an evaporation-rate precaution threshold of 0.2 lb/ft²/hr (0.1 lb/ft²/hr for low-bleed mixes). ACI 305R defines hot weather as 'any combination of high air temperature, low relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation' — not a temperature.
evaluations.advisory_notice: Advisory and contractual. Does not replace the field measurement the referenced standard requires.

constraints.label: Concrete temperature at discharge ≤ 35 °C (95 °F)
constraints.citation_fragment: ACI 301-20 'Specifications for Concrete Construction' and ACI 305.1-14 'Specification for Hot Weather Concreting' limit the maximum concrete temperature to 95 °F (35 °C) at the time of discharge.

constraints.label: ACI 305 evaporation rate ≤ 0.2 lb/ft²/hr
constraints.citation_fragment: Precautions against plastic shrinkage cracking are required when the calculated evaporation rate reaches 0.2 lb/ft²/hr (1.0 kg/m²/h) for conventional concrete, and 0.1 lb/ft²/hr (0.5 kg/m²/h) for low-bleed mixes such as Type 1L blended cements. FHWA states that at ≥ 1.0 kg/m²/h 'definite action to retard evaporation is necessary'. NJDOT MP 29-08 requires placement to be discontinued when the evaporation rate reaches or exceeds 0.15 lb/ft²/hr.

evaluations.trade_display_name: Crew heat exposure — WBGT work/rest and OSHA triggers
evaluations.verdict_summary: Crew heat exposure — WBGT work/rest and OSHA triggers: 72 h bar at 00:00 clips the window 00:00–00:00 (72 h open, 51.75 h productive after the WBGT haircut). Binding constraint: OSHA proposed initial heat trigger — heat index 80 °F.
evaluations.citation: OSHA proposed Heat Injury and Illness Prevention standard (NPRM published 30 August 2024): initial heat trigger is 'a heat index of 80 °F or a wet bulb globe temperature equal to the NIOSH Recommended Action Limit'; high heat trigger is 'heat index of 90 °F or wet bulb globe temperature equal to the NIOSH Recommended Exposure Limit', which requires 'mandatory rest breaks of 15 minutes at least every two hours'. The rule is NOT final — the informal public hearing closed 2 July 2025 and the post-hearing comment period closed 30 October 2025, with no target date announced for a final rule as of mid-2026. In the interim OSHA enforces heat under the General Duty Clause, Section 5(a)(1), and renewed its Heat National Emphasis Program on 10 April 2026 for five further years through 2031. The outdoor WBGT equation is WBGT = 0.7*T_nwb + 0.2*T_globe + 0.1*T_air (OSHA Technical Manual III:4).
evaluations.standard_ref: OSHA Heat Injury and Illness Prevention NPRM (89 FR, 30 Aug 2024); OSHA Technical Manual Section III Ch. 4; ACGIH TLV Heat Stress and Strain (7th ed. documentation, licensed — not reproduced); Liljegren et al. (2008) WBGT model
evaluations.advisory_notice: Advisory and contractual. Does not replace the field measurement the referenced standard requires.

constraints.citation_fragment: OSHA proposed Heat Injury and Illness Prevention rule, initial heat trigger: 'a heat index of 80 °F or a wet bulb globe temperature equal to the NIOSH Recommended Action Limit'. Requires cool drinking water, break areas with cooling measures, acclimatisation protocols for new and returning unacclimatised employees, paid rest breaks if needed to prevent overheating, and regular and effective two-way communication.
